The Art of Note Taking

Note taking is a deceptively simple discipline. The mechanics are easy to describe, but the practice rewards consistent attention to small details that almost no one bothers to track. The notes themselves are the obvious artifact, but the real product is the slow shift in how you read, listen, and pay attention to the world around you.

A good note answers a question its author had not yet finished asking. Writing the note clarifies the question, and the answer that emerges belongs to the writer in a way no quotation ever could. That is the loop that, repeated thousands of times across a career, becomes a body of work worth returning to.

Treat each note as a small act of editing your future thinking. Cut ruthlessly. Link generously. Revisit often. The habit, not the tool, is the thing.
